subject: Portal onboarding — service account egress controls & evidence request
messages:
From: Maria Rios <maria.rios@heliocare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelioCare Procurement <procurement@heliocare.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Portal onboarding: service account egress controls + evidence request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick handoff. We're getting the HelioCare security/infra team aligned to onboard Redwood's Whistic/Vendr profile. A couple of asks to unblock procurement: 

- Can you confirm whether the Redwood service account you provision for portal ingestion has any egress permissions to external S3 buckets (public or customer-controlled)? We need an exported manifest or policy showing allowed egress endpoints.
- If egress is allowed, what controls exist (VPC endpoints, bucket allowlists, VPC peering restrictions)?
- We also need a minimal evidence bundle for CAIQ items A.1.1 / A.2.3 (network egress, outbound encryption) — a fragment is fine.

Procurement is awaiting the egress confirmation to complete their T&Cs. Can you reply with a short statement + attachment, or point us to the policy doc?

Thanks,
Maria Rios
Head of IT Security
HelioCare

[Attachment: internal-note-none — none]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Rios <maria.rios@heliocare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portal onboarding: service account egress controls + evidence request

Maria — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below:

1) Egress: The Redwood "portal-ingest" service account is by default DENIED outbound write access to customer-owned S3 buckets. Outbound network egress is restricted to a small set of managed endpoints (monitoring, telemetry, and signature verification) — all over TLS. We attached the IAM policy and a short writeup.
2) Controls: VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) are used for internal S3 access where applicable, egress is blocked at the VPC NAT for customer VPC deployments. For hosted customers using our API, we enforce allowlists and require customers to opt in to any third-party exports.
3) CAIQ fragments: Attached is a 1‑page fragment covering A.1.1 and A.2.3 plus the service-account IAM policy.

Next steps I propose:
- I will upload the policy PDF to the Whistic/Vendr profile and drop the link here.
- If you want a signed manifest of current outbound endpoints (CSV), we can generate one for audit.

Attachments: redwood-service-account-iam-policy-v1.pdf (policy + explanation)

Let us know whether you need this on our vendor portal or sent by DocuSign for procurement. Happy to hop on a 30 min call if that helps.

— Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales (Vendor Security Lead)
Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0198

Maria / Jordan — looping in a single artifact-and-timeline plan to keep procurement moving. TL;DR: we can produce the CAIQ fragment + an S3 egress manifest within 48 hours if HelioCare confirms scope below.

Scope questions — please confirm which environments you want covered: dev | staging | prod (check all that apply). For procurement the prod slice is usually sufficient, but security sometimes wants the staging snapshot as well.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Day 0 (today): HelioCare confirms prod/staging scope + desired delivery format (Whistic upload vs DocuSign).
- Day 1: Redwood provides CAIQ fragment (A.1.1 / A.2.3), IAM policy PDF, and S3 egress CSV manifest.
- Day 2: Joint 30m review (Redwood infra + HelioCare security) to walk artifacts and confirm acceptance.

Attachments: redwood-mutual-action-plan-template.xlsx 

Note on evidence: our standard S3 egress manifest includes bucket ARNs, allowed endpoints, and a cryptographic timestamp (we can redact ARNs if you prefer anonymized hostnames). Let us know which you prefer.

— Marissa Cole
Manager, Platform Security Outreach
Redwood Inference
